Answer: C
Reason: The initial chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate a massive, well-circumscribed, lobulated opacity occupying the right hemithorax with smooth borders, which is characteristic of a large soft-tissue tumor such as a pleomorphic liposarcoma rather than fluid (effusion), air (pneumothorax), or consolidation (pneumonia). Figure 1c shows the post-operative state following resection of this mass, confirming it was a discrete surgical lesion.
